list.title: OAuth Client Management
list.subtitle: Manage OAuth 2.0 clients for your applications.
list.noTenantHelp: Please select a tenant to view and manage OAuth clients.
list.emptyHelp: Create a new OAuth client to get started.

create.title: Create New Client
create.subtitle: Register a new OAuth2 application for {{tenant}}
create.configHelp: Configure the OAuth2 client settings for your application.
create.important: Important: Make sure to copy your client credentials now. The client secret will not be shown again!

detail.notFound: Client not found or failed to load.

managed.title: Managed by Authway
managed.body: This is the tenant’s account screen client, where users manage their own sign-in. Authway registered it the first time a user of this tenant opened that screen. It cannot be changed or deleted here; it is removed with the tenant.

danger.title: Danger Zone
danger.turnOffHelp: No one can sign in to it and it gets no tokens until it is turned on again. The tokens it holds end.
danger.turnOnHelp: Users can sign in to it again. The sessions it had before it was turned off stay ended.
danger.deleteHelp: Once deleted, this client cannot be recovered. All associated tokens will be invalidated.

turnOffConfirm.title: Turn Client Off
turnOffConfirm.message: No one will be able to sign in to “{{name}}”, and it will get no tokens. The tokens it holds end, and its users’ sessions stay ended when it is turned on again. Continue?

deleteConfirm.title: Delete Client
deleteConfirm.message: Are you sure you want to delete “{{name}}”? This action cannot be undone.

regenerateConfirm.title: Regenerate Client Secret
regenerateConfirm.message: Are you sure you want to regenerate the secret for “{{name}}”? The old secret will immediately stop working.

secretModal.title: New Client Secret
secretModal.warning: Make sure to copy your new client secret now. You won’t be able to see it again!

validation.grantRequired: At least one Grant Type is required
validation.scopeRequired: At least one Scope is required
validation.providerRequired: Choose at least one way to sign in
validation.redirectRequired: At least one Redirect URI is required for Authorization Code
validation.originsRequired: Public clients with Authorization Code need at least one Allowed Origin for browser CORS
validation.audience: Each audience must be a distinct identifier without spaces, at most 255 characters
validation.httpsUrl: Enter one absolute https URL without a fragment (#…)

form.name: Client Name *
form.homePageHelp: Where users go back to from Authway’s screens (the account screen, an accepted invitation when there is no sign-in start URL). https only.
form.logoHelp: Shown with the application’s name on the sign-in and consent screens. https only.
form.descriptionPlaceholder: Enter a description for the client
form.initiateLoginHelp: Where the application starts a sign-in. A user who accepts an invitation to this application is sent here with iss and login_hint, and the application sends them on to Authway. https only. Empty: they go to the home page.
form.redirectUrisHelp: Enter each URI on a new line.
form.redirectUrisHelpM2m: Not used by machine-to-machine clients — leave empty unless you add a redirect-based grant.
form.postLogoutHelp: Enter each URI on a new line. Sign-out may only return to one of these addresses (exact match). If empty, Redirect URIs will be used.
form.originsHelpRequired: Enter each browser origin on a new line (scheme + host + port, no path). Required for a public client using Authorization Code, so the reverse proxy can validate cross-origin token requests.
form.originsHelp: Enter each browser origin on a new line. Only needed for a public client (SPA) using Authorization Code — a native app called back on http://127.0.0.1/… or its own URI scheme needs none.
form.audienceHelp: Enter the identifier of each API this client’s access tokens are for, one per line (usually the API’s URL). They become the token’s aud claim, which the API checks for its own identifier. Empty: the tokens name no API.
form.backchannelHelp: For an application that keeps its own server-side session: a logout token is POSTed here whenever a session of one of its users ends. Must be a public https address — the call is made from the server, not from a browser. Empty: the application is not told.
form.skipConsentHelp: Bypass the OAuth consent screen on login. Enable only for first-party / trusted clients you control — never for third-party apps.
form.skipLogoutConsentHelp: Bypass the logout confirmation screen. Recommended together with Skip Consent Screen for first-party clients.
form.tokenFormatHelp: JWT lets a resource server validate this client’s tokens offline via OIDC discovery (JWKS) — but a resource server that validates it offline keeps accepting it until it expires, even after the user signs out or is suspended. Leave on Default unless an API needs offline validation.
form.publicHelp: Select for SPAs or mobile apps that cannot securely store a Client Secret.
